subject.title: No migration path or warning when a model provider id is removed/renamed (openai-codex -> openai): OAuth profiles silently orphaned

question: Should this issue remain a separate diagnostic-hint tracker, or should it close only after the Nix-mode doctor/auth repair blocker is fixed and verified?
rationale: The code already has an automatic auth-profile migration when `doctor --fix` runs, but the reported install could not reach that path and the direct wording-only PR closed unmerged because the wording may mislead users about automatic migration.

options.title: Keep Until Reachability And Guidance Are Verified
options.body: Keep this issue open until the Nix-mode blocker is fixed or rejected and the doctor output either proves automatic migration is discoverable or gains a precise hint.

options.title: Fold Into The Broader Migration Plan
options.body: Move the remaining wording and proof requirement into the broader legacy Codex migration-plan work and close this only after that canonical path is viable.

options.title: Close After Nix-Mode Fix Lands
options.body: If maintainers decide the existing auth-profile migration is sufficient once `doctor --fix` can run, close this after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95135 is fixed with proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Until Reachability And Guidance Are Verified
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the Nix-mode blocker is fixed or rejected and the doctor output either proves automatic migration is discoverable or gains a precise hint.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns much of the OpenAI provider unification and auth migration history that determines whether this should be a separate diagnostic or part of the canonical migration contract.
